title: **The Go struct-field rule is patched locally** — when the Go grammar loads, its repeated one-line struct-field rule is replaced with the rule [worlpaker/go-syntax#25](https://github.com/worlpaker/go-syntax/pull/25) merged, because the vend...

attrs.text: **The Go struct-field rule is patched locally** — when the Go grammar loads, its repeated one-line struct-field rule is replaced with the rule [worlpaker/go-syntax#25](https://github.com/worlpaker/go-syntax/pull/25) merged, because the vendored rule backtracks exponentially on lines such as a brace-bearing comment after `struct {`. If a dependency upgrade removes that rule, loading the grammar throws and Go code renders as plain text; delete the patch once `@shikijs/langs` ships the upstream rule.

title: **The Perl match rule is patched locally** — when the Perl grammar loads, its bare `/…/` match rule also begins after `,`, `!`, `=`, `=>` and after `split`, `grep`, `and`, `or`, `not`, `return`, `while` and `until`, because the vendored rul...

attrs.text: **The Perl match rule is patched locally** — when the Perl grammar loads, its bare `/…/` match rule also begins after `,`, `!`, `=`, `=>` and after `split`, `grep`, `and`, `or`, `not`, `return`, `while` and `until`, because the vendored rule treats a pattern such as `split /^---\s*$/m, $text` as code and colors the rest of the source as a string. These words and `if`/`unless` count only when no identifier character, sigil, `>`, `:` or `-` precedes them, so `$split / 2` and `$obj->return / 2` are divisions. A `/` elsewhere, such as after `?`, `[` or `print`, still reads as division. The upstream [textmate/perl.tmbundle](https://github.com/textmate/perl.tmbundle) grammar has the same rule. If a dependency upgrade changes that rule, loading the grammar throws and Perl code renders as plain text.

title: **A long highlighted fence retains its complete token DOM** — streaming avoids re-parsing, re-tokenizing, and reconciling the completed prefix, but it does not discard old colors or virtualize token spans. Final DOM cardinality therefore st...

attrs.text: **A long highlighted fence retains its complete token DOM** — streaming avoids re-parsing, re-tokenizing, and reconciling the completed prefix, but it does not discard old colors or virtualize token spans. Final DOM cardinality therefore still follows the fence's token count; nested/container fences and a pathological single long line remain on the general tail path.

title: **Math copies as TeX only within one Markdown document** — a selection that reaches outside its `MarkdownText` root, such as from a user message into a reply, keeps the browser's native copy, which joins KaTeX's hidden MathML text with the ...

attrs.text: **Math copies as TeX only within one Markdown document** — a selection that reaches outside its `MarkdownText` root, such as from a user message into a reply, keeps the browser's native copy, which joins KaTeX's hidden MathML text with the visible glyphs. Inside one document, the plain text of non-math content comes from `innerText`, so code-block language labels and copy-button text are included, as in native copy.

title: **Diff fences infer colors per file and per side** — `diff` and `patch` fences parse hunk line budgets so later file headers stay chrome, tokenize each file's removed and added lines separately with the language its `---`/`+++` header names...

attrs.text: **Diff fences infer colors per file and per side** — `diff` and `patch` fences parse hunk line budgets so later file headers stay chrome, tokenize each file's removed and added lines separately with the language its `---`/`+++` header names, and leave the body plain when that path is unknown. A streaming diff re-tokenizes on every chunk; the marker column stays in copied source.

title: **Overlong lines stay uncolored** — a source line of 1,000 or more UTF-16 units renders as one plain run in every highlighted surface, because TextMate scanning cost grows superlinearly with line length and a single generated line can other...

attrs.text: **Overlong lines stay uncolored** — a source line of 1,000 or more UTF-16 units renders as one plain run in every highlighted surface, because TextMate scanning cost grows superlinearly with line length and a single generated line can otherwise block the page for seconds. The grammar state skips that line, so a comment or template literal that opens or closes on it mis-colors the following lines. Highlighting still runs synchronously during render, so a file with thousands of ordinary lines costs proportionally more.

title: **Bare URLs end before non-ASCII punctuation** — the [tokenizer patch](../../../patches/micromark-extension-gfm-autolink-literal@2.1.0.patch) and the [transform patch](../../../patches/mdast-util-gfm-autolink-literal@2.0.1.patch) end a GFM ...

attrs.text: **Bare URLs end before non-ASCII punctuation** — the [tokenizer patch](../../../patches/micromark-extension-gfm-autolink-literal@2.1.0.patch) and the [transform patch](../../../patches/mdast-util-gfm-autolink-literal@2.0.1.patch) end a GFM autolink literal at non-ASCII punctuation, symbols, or whitespace, so a URL with an unencoded character such as `（` or `・` in its path links only up to it; write such a URL as `<…>` or `[…](…)`. A URL followed directly by CJK letters still links them, because paths such as `/wiki/中文` are valid. Both patches are keyed to exact versions: an upgrade of either package must re-apply or retire its patch, otherwise the boundary rule silently disappears.
